title: ld-preload-and-libmix-breadcrumbs
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal breadcrumb file for a recurring class of failures where containerized inference jobs hit CUDA OOMs or fail early with driver/runtime mismatch errors. Goal: capture commands, observed outputs, minimal repro flags used, and running hypotheses so the next time I see it I don't start from scratch.

Symptom clusters observed (across several incidents):
- Immediate startup failures with messages like:
  - 'CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version'
  - 'libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory' (but nvidia-smi works on host)
  - 'RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate X GiB' even on a single small tensor run that previously worked
  - weird segfaults inside cuBLAS/cuDNN causing the Python process to die without Python-level exception (segfault on cublasLtMatmul)
- Failures often correlate with: host driver updated recently, container base image updated, or a host-level LD_PRELOAD trick used by infra (profilers, jemalloc, nvtx shim).

Commands I run (keeps the exact flags so I can copy-paste):
- Host checks:
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name --format=csv\  # quick host driver version check
  - cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || true
  - ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 || true
  - ldconfig -p | grep libcuda || true

- Container introspection (when I can exec into pod/container):
  - docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint bash IMAGE -c "nvidia-smi; ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.*/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep cuda || true"\  # check which libcuda the torch binary links to
  - readelf -d /usr/local/lib/python3.*/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep NEEDED || true
  - python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory)'

- Dynamic tracing for library resolution issues:
  - LD_DEBUG=libs python script.py 2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'
  - strace -f -e open,openat -s 200 -o /tmp/strace.out python script.py && tail -n 200 /tmp/strace.out | grep libcuda || true
  - ldd $(python -c "import torch; import os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(torch.__file__), 'lib','libtorch_cuda.so'))")

- Repro with minimal program to rule out caching/batch logic:
  - small reproducible file repro_min.py:
    import torch
    a = torch.randn(1024, 1024, device='cuda')
    b = torch.randn(1024, 1024, device='cuda')
    c = a @ b
    print(c.sum().item())
  - Run with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to surface async errors:
    CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python repro_min.py

Common outputs I've captured (snippets):
- 'CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version' from import torch (happens before allocating anything)
- 'RuntimeError: CUDA error: initialization error' sometimes followed by a stack trace into driver API calls
- 'RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.50 GiB (GPU 0; 7.79 GiB total capacity; 5.23 GiB already allocated; 0.00 GiB free; 6.18 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)' but nvidia-smi shows GPU free memory ~100MiB then spikes after process exit
- 'Fatal error: ../third_party/cublas/include/cublas_v2.h: xx: cuBLAS status INVALID_VALUE' (appears only with certain image combos)

Hypotheses (ranked by how often they explain the incidents):
1) Host-driver vs. runtime ABI mismatch: host driver too old/new for CUDA runtime shipped in the container (classic 'driver < runtime' or reverse if shimbed libs).
   - Evidence: 'driver version is insufficient' message; fixed temporarily by running with --gpus=all on nodes with matching driver version.
2) LD_PRELOAD or host-provided libcuda being shadowed by container libs (or vice versa). Some infra setups mount /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu or preload profiling libs which break symbol resolutions.\   - Evidence: LD_DEBUG shows libcuda resolved from host mount point even though container has its own /usr/local/cuda/lib64; fixed when removing LD_PRELOAD or unmounting host path.
3) Mixed CUDA runtime libraries between Python package (torch compiled against CUDA 12.2) and system libs (cuBLAS/cuDNN) from different minor versions leading to undefined symbols/segfaults.
4) Memory accounting differences: container or runtime uses a memory allocator (jemalloc, tcmalloc) that fragments the GPU-visible allocations leading to OOM at small allocations while nvidia-smi reports plenty of memory.

Things I've tried that helped / didn't help:
- Rebuilt the image with cuDNN and CUDA runtime that exactly match host driver minor version -> helped in 3/5 cases.
- Unsetting LD_PRELOAD or removing the profiler shim from env -> immediately fixed a couple of cases; big clue when removal correlates with success.
- Forcing the container to use host libcuda by bind-mounting /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 into container -> in one case this fixed 'driver insufficient' but in another it caused segfaults (probable ABI mismatch).
- Downgrading PyTorch wheel to match system CUDA -> costly but reproduced fix.
- Adding torch.cuda.empty_cache() and reducing batch sizes -> mitigates OOM but not root cause for initialization errors.

Minimal triage checklist (for quick run on new incident):
1) ssh to node; run nvidia-smi and cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
2) docker exec into container or run a debug image with same mounts; check ldd/readelf on the CUDA-linked libs used by the process
3) LD_PRELOAD? printenv | grep -i preload; unset and retry
4) Run repro_min.py with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and LD_DEBUG=libs to see which libcuda is picked up and whether initialization errors occur synchronously
5) If segfault: capture coredump (ulimit -c unlimited) and run gdb on binary to see which shared object triggered crash (use 'info sharedlibrary' in gdb)
6) If OOM but nvidia-smi reports free memory: try running with PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 or set allocator flags (TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6) to test fragmentation hypothesis

Notes for infra team (to escalate if recurring across cluster):
- If host images apply LD_PRELOAD or mount host /usr/lib paths into containers, add a test in node bootstrap that runs a small CUDA program in an isolated container and verifies driver/runtime compatibility (fail auto-upgrades if mismatch detected).\- Prefer installing matching libcuda on nodes via NV driver packages instead of bind-mounting host libs into containers.
- Add a node-level health check in cluster autoscaler to report 'cuda-runtime-abi-compatible' label so scheduling can avoid mismatched nodes for GPU workloads.

Repro timeline for the last incident (2025-02-28):
- 09:03 Job A started; immediately logs 'CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version'
- 09:07 I SSH to node; host driver shows 535.86
- 09:10 Container image built w/ CUDA 12.2 runtime; python imports fail
- 09:20 Exec into container; LD_DEBUG shows libcuda resolved to /host-mount/usr/lib/libcuda.so.1 (host had old shim copied during node upgrade)
- 09:40 Unmounted host lib dir and restarted container -> job imports succeed; run repro_min.py -> passes
- 09:50 Notified infra to remove host mount from node image; ticket JIRA-RT-4321 opened

Future quick hacks to avoid production impact:
- Canary image with 'compatibility probe' script that fails fast on node if mismatch detected (script runs python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda)' and checks exit code)
- Short-term: set up a wrapper that unsets LD_PRELOAD in the job environment unless explicitly opted-in

Open questions to investigate further:
- How often do jemalloc/tcmalloc-based host allocators affect GPU-visible fragmentation? Any measurable correlation?
- Are there cases where driver reports match but cuBLAS minor version mismatch still causes silent incorrect results? Need fuzz tests across minor versions.

Scratch area - commands & outputs I scribbled during incident (raw):
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name --format=csv\driver_version, name\535.86, A100-SXM4-80GB
$ docker run --rm --gpus all my-image:sha nvidia-smi\Fri Feb 28 09:03:21 2025\+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86       CUDA Version: 12.0     |
|-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+

LD_DEBUG=libs python repro_min.py 2>&1 | head -n 80\\=> attempt to open /host-mount/usr/lib/libcuda.so.1 => succeeded
python repro_min.py error snippet:
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version

strace output snippet:
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/host-mount/usr/lib/libcuda.so.1", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3

-- end of scratch --

If I can't fix it quickly: escalate with these artifacts: repro_min.py, LD_DEBUG dump, strace open list, host nvidia-smi output, and the container image id + node bootstrap image id.

Todo (me):
- Turn this checklist into a tiny CLI tool 'gpu-compat-check' that runs inside debug container and prints PASS/FAIL plus suggested remedial step.
- Add small unit test to repro-kernels repo that attempts loading torch with several libcuda permutations to capture flaky combinations.

Last run notes: today (2025-03-05) I ran the compat probe on 4 nodes; 1 node had host-mount causing libcuda to resolve to a shim. Confirmed the fix and removed the mount.

-- end of document --
